approval_required_for: Any architecture or design-space change beyond the selected trusted template and approved parameter bindings.
Any change to declared pipeline structure, stage boundaries, buffering, flow control, tiling, transfer order, or latency contract rather than a bounded implementation correction within that contract.
Any memory-layout, DDR address-map, transfer-unit, memory-scheduling, or runtime ABI change.

Any numeric-policy, rounding, saturation, cast-point, accumulator-precision, comparison-policy, or tolerance change. The current repair loop must instead preserve these identities; a change requires terminating and re-contracting the loop, and tolerance may not be loosened to force a pass.
Any major template substitution, free-form RTL rewrite, or repair outside the localized causal cone.
Any change to the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper or board-target identity. Such a change requires a new approved discovery/contract cycle; a simplified substitute remains forbidden.
Any ambiguous board or app-shell target selection that cannot be resolved from cited sample-project artifacts and real tool evidence.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block this specialist handoff and refine only the failed debug-contract fields. Preserve unrelated passing Stage 6 static evidence; do not waive a checker, weaken trace requirements, alter immutable semantic identities, or claim a hardware defect.
executable_actions.rationale: Create the four checker-bound handoff artifacts that convert every failed checker into a canonical boundary trace, earliest localization, bounded replay, minimal causal context, and scoped certificate decision without hardcoded case names.

consumes: bound loader/harness hashes and executed complete-scope DUT weight-consumption evidence
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the affected certificate reuse_allowed=false. Classify missing or mismatched identity/evidence as stale or unsupported and rerun only the exact missing gate on the immutable checkpoint and stimulus. Do not issue a hardware backtrack unless a separate canonical higher-layer trace and targeted replay satisfy the certificate challenge policy.
produces: current-contract operator-leaf promotion certificate or scoped non-reuse diagnosis
current-contract single-layer promotion certificate or scoped non-reuse diagnosis
executable_actions.rationale: The supplied certificates are present but non-reusable under the current semantic-evidence contract. Revalidate their exact evidence before reuse, without treating staleness as a causal contradiction or blindly reopening every lower-layer tool run.

consumes: failed checker native log, command, tool version, exit status, and artifact hashes
current immutable checkpoint, full tensor catalog, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy, tolerance, and semantic-testbench identities
exact sample-project wrapper and simulation-source hashes when the failure is in layer three
executable_actions.on_failure: Record a checker, golden-reference, trace-instrumentation, or adapter capability blocker and keep the current layer unpromoted. Do not fabricate cycles or expected values, infer hardware correctness from a static failure, patch a downstream symptom, or expand immediately to an unrestricted waveform or full-stack rerun.
produces: SACG failure lesson bound to the failed checker and violated constraints
executable_actions.rationale: Ensure any failed checker at any of the three verification layers is converted from native tool output into a case-adapter-independent boundary trace and compact earliest-causal slice before a repair agent is invoked.

executable_actions.on_failure: If replay is non-reproducing or challenge criteria are incomplete, leave lower certificates unchanged and classify the current failure as unresolved. If identities differ, mark evidence stale rather than contradicted. Never generate an unscoped backtrack request or reopen all lower-layer evidence.
produces: optional scoped stage backtrack request naming the affected certificate, boundary cone, transaction, and replay evidence
executable_actions.rationale: Reproduce the earliest violation under immutable identities and decide whether the current layer owns the failure or a precisely named lower certificate is contradicted. The decision must prevent broad reopening.

consumes: immutable checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy, tolerance, and semantic-testbench identities
executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at the operator-leaf layer and feed new tool output back through localization. Do not promote to the connected layer. Stop and request approval rather than changing architecture, declared pipeline structure, numeric policy, or a major template.
produces: bounded leaf repair patch manifest with changed DUT source hashes
executable_actions.rationale: Authorize a downstream leaf repair only when localization routes the earliest violation to a named operator or leaf module. This specialist supplies the repair boundary but does not directly patch RTL.

executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at the single-layer closure and repeat tool-output-to-localization. If replay instead contradicts a leaf certificate, stop this repair and issue only the scoped lower-layer challenge. Any change to declared pipeline structure, buffering policy, tiling, transfer order, or latency contract requires approval.
executable_actions.rationale: Authorize connected-kernel repair only when all required leaf certificates are current and the reproducing earliest violation is at a merge, residual alignment, cast, beat/order, or handshake boundary inside the connected single-transformer-layer kernel.

consumes: current valid operator-leaf and single-layer certificates
exact user-supplied wrapper and simulation-source hashes
complete Transformer-block DDR input and weight image hashes
executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at third-layer functional closure and return new real-tool evidence to localization; do not proceed to Vivado, bitstream, or board runtime. Do not replace or modify the exact sample-project wrapper, loosen tolerance, change the golden, or alter memory layout/runtime ABI without approval. If the earliest violation moves into a lower certified scope, stop and apply the scoped challenge policy.
produces: bounded third-layer integration, loader, harness, instrumentation, or approved-structure pipeline repair manifest
refreshed AXI, DDR, liveness, order, and board semantic evidence
executable_actions.rationale: Authorize third-layer repair only when lower semantic certificates are current and the earliest reproducing violation lies in the multilayer pipeline, exact sample-project integration, AXI protocol, DDR image, address map, loader, transfer, or runtime interface. The exact wrapper and semantic golden identities remain immutable.

observations: The declared verification hierarchy follows the required order: operator leaf modules, connected single-transformer-layer kernel, then the exact board AXI/DDR wrapped system. Promotion and repair must stop at the first failed layer.

The Stage 6 verification artifact contract has status pass, and later deadlock-watchdog, implementation-package, and board-runtime executions are correctly classified as downstream obligations rather than current-stage failures.

The role slice reports that debug trace and localization schemas and 13 boundary contracts exist. Detailed checker rows may be omitted by policy, so their omission is not treated as a failed checker. The four specialist output artifacts are nevertheless not listed in the supplied artifact inventory and must be materialized for the handoff.

The visible verification DAG models success dependencies but does not expose checker-failure edges to trace capture, localization, replay, and bounded repair. The cross-layer failure routing matrix must add those failure edges for every checker at all three layers.

The visible common trace fields cover cycle, boundary, transaction, tile, logical index, observed value, expected value, contract, and status. The full schemas must additionally require or reference checker/run identity, raw evidence hash, tool command and version, layer and source kind, contract version, event ordering, immutable semantic identities, run-bound implementation identities, and expected-value provenance. Static checker failures must use artifact/tool boundary events with no fabricated hardware cycle.

Typed trace payloads must preserve cross-layer facts: model and shape indices; pre-cast and post-cast numeric values with immutable policy and tolerance hashes; transaction, tile, sequence, lane, beat, valid, ready, last, and latency facts; memory address, burst, offset, image-region, and transfer-count facts; runtime register and ABI facts; DUT/elaboration and loader/harness hashes; and, at layer three, exact sample-project wrapper and simulation-source hashes.

Expected values in a boundary trace may come only from the independent target-model reference for the same checkpoint and stimulus or from an explicit protocol, shape, liveness, address, or ordering contract. They may not be random, inferred from DUT output, or produced by an identity/default model.

Earliest violation means the first failing event in topological boundary order and transaction/sequence/beat order for which the nearest causal predecessor is demonstrated to pass. For a value failure it is the first tolerance-qualified mismatch; for order or protocol it is the first illegal or missing transfer; for liveness it is the first unmet deadline tied to the last progress and first blocked handshake, not merely the final watchdog cycle; for a static failure it is the first violated artifact dependency or binding with its raw tool evidence hash.

The targeted replay contract must select the failing checker, transaction, tile, logical range, beat or address range, bounded cycle/event window, nearest passing predecessor, violating boundary, and at most the next consumer required to disambiguate causality. It must preserve checkpoint, full tensor catalog, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy, tolerance, semantic testbench contract, and exact board-wrapper hashes. Trace expansion must proceed one boundary radius at a time rather than defaulting to a full-stack rerun.

The minimal repair context must contain the failed checker and constraints, immutable semantic identity bundle, run-bound DUT/elaboration and loader/harness identities, raw evidence hashes, earliest violation and nearest passing predecessor, compact causal path, expected-value provenance, allowed repair target and source/template hashes, forbidden immutable artifacts, exact replay command and selectors, certificate impact, and approval boundary. Unrelated waveforms, modules, and cleanup must be excluded.

Failure routing must distinguish capability and hardware causes. Missing target-model inference, incomplete tensor coverage, absent bound weight-consumption evidence, missing trace instrumentation, or an incapable checker is a checker, golden-reference, loader, or harness blocker and is not hardware-correctness evidence. A real-tool value, order, liveness, address, or protocol failure may route to hardware repair only after earliest causal localization.

The routing matrix must map an internal operator or leaf-boundary divergence to bounded leaf/template repair; a first divergence at a leaf merge, residual alignment, cast, connected-kernel beat/order, or connected-kernel handshake to single-layer pipeline repair; a multilayer ordering/liveness failure to the third-layer multilayer subgate; and a wrapper, AXI, DDR image, address map, loader, runtime ABI, or transfer failure to board integration or memory/runtime repair. A board-layer symptom must not be patched downstream when its bound earliest violation lies inside a lower layer.

A higher-layer failure may challenge a lower-layer certificate only when the lower certificate is current-contract-valid, the higher-layer checker has executed, the canonical trace and raw evidence hashes validate, all fixed semantic identities match, the certified lower DUT/elaboration and loader/harness identities match, the boundary contract and mapping versions match, the earliest violating boundary lies inside the certified scope with a passing predecessor, and targeted replay reproduces the contradiction. Only the named certificate, module, boundary cone, transaction, and dependent promotion edge may be reopened.

A missing identity, changed DUT or harness, stale contract version, changed checkpoint/stimulus/reference/testbench/wrapper identity, non-reproducing replay, or failure located before the lower scope is not a certificate contradiction. It makes prior evidence non-reusable or leaves the current-layer failure unresolved, but it cannot authorize broad reopening.

The authoritative certificate validator marks both supplied lower-layer certificates current_contract_valid=false and reuse_allowed=false under spatialaccagent.real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2. Their historical Stage 7 pass outcomes therefore cannot be consumed as current promotion evidence. Because no contradicting bound trace is supplied, no lower-layer causal backtrack should be opened; bounded current-contract revalidation is required instead.

The absent board AXI/DDR promotion certificate and pending functional, Vivado, bitstream, and board-runtime evidence are downstream obligations. They do not invalidate the otherwise passing Stage 6 static plan, but no final or hardware pass may be claimed until those gates execute successfully.

All trace, reference, tensor-coverage, replay, and certificate scopes must stop at Transformer-block boundaries. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail work must not be added to DUT golden or required weight-consumption scope.

The authoritative SACG-memory truth in the supplied state reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. Historical ready outcomes are evidence history only and do not override current certificate validation.
proposed_actions: Materialize the four expected Stage 6 artifacts and run the declared boundary, localization, replay, causal-context, repair-boundary, data-order, artifact-hash, and human-boundary checkers before aggregate handoff.

Register every verification checker with a canonical failure adapter that emits a common envelope plus typed semantic, order, liveness, protocol, memory, runtime, or static-contract payload. If a checker cannot emit or trigger such evidence, classify the gap as verifier capability work rather than hardware failure.

Revalidate the stale operator-leaf and single-layer certificates against the current real-weight semantic-evidence contract. Reuse matching raw evidence where every required hash and tool record is complete; rerun only missing or stale gates and do not issue a causal backtrack without a reproducing bound trace.

For each future checker failure, perform boundary bisection, identify the earliest violation and nearest passing predecessor, generate a bounded replay selector, execute the failed checker replay under immutable identities, and package only the causal repair cone.

Issue a lower-layer certificate challenge only when all conjunctive challenge criteria pass. Otherwise retain unaffected lower certificates, classify identity mismatch as stale/non-reusable, and repair or investigate the current layer.

Dispatch bounded repair to exactly one routed scope, then rerun the targeted failed checker and the semantic aggregate for that layer. Do not promote to the next layer or proceed to Vivado while the current layer remains failed.
risks: Current specialist handoff risk: without the routing matrix, replay gate, challenge policy, and minimal-context contract as checker-bound artifacts, downstream agents could interpret the general debug policy inconsistently even though the base Stage 6 artifact contract passed.

The visible targeted_replay_outputs list omits the replay plan and causal path even though the repair handoff requires them. If the full contract does not reconcile this difference, a failed checker could produce localization without an executable replay.
If immutable semantic and run-bound identity hashes are not present in the canonical trace manifest, unrelated or stale higher-layer evidence could incorrectly challenge a lower certificate.

If liveness, data-order, AXI, and DDR failures are forced into only observed_value and expected_value fields without typed protocol payloads, earliest-cause localization may collapse into generic waveform debugging.

Treating the two stale certificates as contradicted hardware evidence would cause broad reopening without a bound trace; treating their historical pass summaries as reusable would allow invalid promotion evidence.

Repairing a board output symptom without proving whether corruption first occurred in the multilayer kernel, AXI transfer, DDR image, loader, runtime ABI, or wrapper boundary could alter the wrong layer.

Changing numeric policy, tolerance, checkpoint, target-model reference, stimulus, semantic testbench, or exact sample-project wrapper during replay would contaminate the repair loop and invalidate causal comparison.
A trace or replay that includes model-tail operations or requires their weights would expand the accelerator scope beyond Transformer blocks and contaminate semantic certificate coverage.
Pending deadlock, implementation, and board-runtime gates may later fail, but reporting them now as current-stage checker failures would violate the supplied stage-gate policy.
Any repair that changes architecture, declared pipeline structure, memory layout, runtime ABI, numeric policy, or a major template without approval would exceed this specialist's decision authority.

edges: current higher-layer bound trace -> scoped lower-layer certificate challenge
current valid lower-layer certificate + no contradicting bound trace -> certificate reuse
stale or identity-mismatched certificate -> bounded revalidation without causal challenge

output.summary: The supplied Stage 6 contract correctly declares the bottom-up three-layer repair order, reusable-but-challengeable certificates, case-adapter-independent tracing, and prohibition on broad reopening. However, the four specialist handoff artifacts are not listed as produced, and the visible debug contract does not yet prove a uniform failed-checker route containing immutable run identity, typed value/order/liveness/protocol evidence, earliest-violation semantics, bounded replay, minimal repair context, and a checker-enforced certificate challenge decision. Existing operator-leaf and single-layer certificates are non-reusable because the authoritative current validator marks them stale for the current semantic-evidence contract; that is not a contradicting trace and must not trigger broad backtrack. No active SACG-memory contamination barrier, retry request, or backtrack request is reported.
